1	# Changelog
2	### February 19th 2026: WanGP v10.951, Breaking the Sound Barrier, Mach 2
3	Here comes the (last ?) missing bit in WanGP of the *Text To Speech* offering: **emotions**
4	
5	There isnt many TTS models around that let you express emotions, so I hope you will forgive me for adding an old TTS model (6 months old!) in WanGP: **Index TTS 2**.
6	
7	But in WanGP, you wont just get the vanilla version of Index TTS:
8	- *Two speakers Dialogue* (with 2 Cloned Voices) out of the Box
9	- Each speaker can express *varrying emotions* within the same prompt   
10	- *Volume Normalization* of the two speaker voices (no one will speak louder)
11	- Optimized for a *dialogue that can last forever* (new *infinitalk* best friend)
12	- *GPU Poor version*: VRAM, 6GB will be sufficient
13	- Highly Optimized with *vllm* & *Cuda Graph acceleration*: *up to 10x faster* than vanilla Index TTS. On high end GPUs, generating a 1 min of dialogue will take only 30s !
14	
15	Here is how to use it: By default Index TTS, will detect automatically the emotion to apply to a Text Prompt based on the text itself. However, it will apply the same emotion for the whole prompt. If you want a different emotion per sentence, just insert empty lines between each sentence.
16	
17	You can also set manually which emotion you expect with [] tags, here is one example for one speaker:
18	```bash
19	[fear] At the very beginning I was so afraid to speak.
20	[sadness] Nobody would talk to me. I felt so alone.
21	[disgust] They would just ignore me and pretend that I didnt exist
22	[happy] By chance I discovered this wonderful App, and now everything is different.
23	[anger] I have a new voice and now everybody will have no choice but to listen to my words !!! 
24	```
25	You can mix emotions *[sadness,disgust]* or if you want to precise the weight of one or several emotions *[sadness=0.7,disgust]* (in any case total of weights is 1)
26	
27	Remember two speakers mode requires to insert *"Speaker 1:"* & *"Speaker 2:"* to indicate who is talking.
28	
29	There is only one snag: Index TTS 2 supports only English & Chinese. But dont' panic ! not all is lost. There is a workaround:
30	1) Feed *Index TTS 2* with the voice to clone and ask it to generate a sample English spoken text with with the emotion you expected
31	2) Now ask *Qwen3TTS*, to clone this newly generated voice sample (in English) in the other language you want
32	
33	
34	### February 16th 2026: WanGP v10.9, Breaking the Sound Barrier
35	With this new release of WanGP you should have the best TTS (Text To Speech) experience you can find:
36	
37	- **Qwen3 TTS Powered Up**:  
38	   - with new *Cuda Graph* optimized mode, speech generation is up to *4x faster*, in some occasion generating 1s of speech may take less than 1s !
39	   - with int8 quantization, the Qwen3 TTS can work at full speed with only 6 GB of VRAM
40	   - New **Two Speakers Mode** with **Two Cloned Voices** can generate dialogues with much smoother transitions than with *Kugel Audio* 
41	
42	- **Heart Mula Powered Up**:
43	   - with new *Cuda Graph* optimized mode, song generation is up to 6x faster
44	
45	- **Ace Step 1.5 Powered Up**:
46	   - WanGP version offers an exclusive support for *vllm* & *int8 quantization* for LM (that is fast LM & low VRAM at the same time)
47	   - you will only need 10GB of RAM and 6 GB oF VRAM, to run Ace Step with all its features
48	
49	Also you now have a choice of multiple *Prompt Enhancements* for *Qwen3 TTS* & *Kugel Audio*: *Prompt Enhancer* can now generate for you either a *Monologue* or a *Dialogue between two Speakers*
50	
51	Please note that to use the new *Cuda Graph*, mode you will need to select either *vllm* or *cuda graph* in *Configuration / Performance / Language Models Decoder Engine*. Profiles 1,3  or 3+ will need to be enabled for the corresponding Model. vllm is a powered up version of cuda graph that may not always work with all GPUs. But don't worry if it is not available for your GPU there will be an automatic fallback to cuda graph.
52	
53	### February 12th 2026: WanGP v10.84, Easy Metal
54	
55	- **Ace Step 1.5 Turbo Super Charged**: all the best features of *Ace Step 1.5* are now in *WanGP* and are *Fast* & *Easy* to use:
56	   * Manual Selection of *Bpm*, *Keyscale*, *Time Signature* & *Language*
57	   * Use *LM* to auto detect *Bpm*, *Keyscale*, *Time Signature* & *Language* that best suits your *Lyrics*
58	   * Use *LM* to refine *Music Caption* or auto detect *Song Duration*
59	   * Choice of *vllm* engine for *LM* for up to *10x faster LM generation!!!*. Also as a WanGP exclusive, *vllm* is offered in *INT8 quantized* format for lower VRAM requirements. Please note you will need to install *Triton* and *Flash Attention 2* (check the *INSTALLATION.Md* for easy install)
60	   * Use *LM* to refine *Music Caption* (usually the key to get the song theme you expected)
61	   * UI Makeover to better match vocabulary used in original Ace Step App (but without its complexity...)
62	   * Refined *System Prompt* used in *Prompt Enhancer* to generate *Lyrics* (I recommend to use the *LLama Joy Prompt Enhancer*)
63	
64	- **LoKr support**: this "Lora" like format has been tested with *Flux Klein 9B*
65	
66	- **Optimized Int8 Kernels**: all the *Quantized INT8 checkpoints* (most of the quantized checkpoints) used with WanGP should be now *10% faster !!!*. You will need to install *Triton*. It is experimental, so for the moment it needs to be enabled manually in the *Config / Performance* tab. Please share your feedback on *discord* by mentioning your GPU so that I know if it works properly.
67	
68	- **Auto Queue Saved if Gen Error**: if for whatever reason you have got an error during a Gen, the queue will now be automatically saved. So you can try again this queue later (with a different config or when the related bug is fixed, if ever ...).
69	
70	- **UI Updates** (thx *Tophness!*):
71	Updated the *Self-Refiner UI* to a dynamic, slider-based interface (no more manual text input).
72	Improved queue reordering: items can now be dragged and dropped directly onto the Top and Bottom buttons while rearranging the queue in order to snap scroll to the top and bottom.
73	
74	- **Kugel Audio Audio Split**: Kugel Audio is a great model but strangely it tends to accelerate with long speeches. In order to avoid this effect, we need to split audio speeches. You can either do that manually by inserting an *Empty Line* or by specifiying an *Auto Audio Split Duration* (don't worry WanGP will try to split between lines or sentences). 
75	
76	*update 10.81*: Fixes\
77	*update 10.82*: UI update\
78	*update 10.83*: Kugel Audio Split\
79	*update 10.84*: Ace Step RAM optimizations (fixed memory leak & reduce RAM requirements)
80	
81	**Note to RTX 50xx owners**: you will need to upgrade to *pytorch 2.10* (see upgrade procedure below) to be able to use *Triton*
82	
83	### February 4rd 2026: WanGP v10.70, Let's Get Ready To Rumble !
84	*The competition between Open Source & Close Source has never been that hot !*
85	
86	- **Ace Step 1.5 Turbo**: this long waited open source project claims to have overthrown *Suno 5*. It lets you generate high multi minutes quality songs. It comes in four flavours: *Vanilla* (No Language Model Preprocessing, **4s Generation Time!!!**) & *3 levels of LM Preprocessing* for a higher Quality (and increasing VRAM requirements)
87	
88	Please note that when using the *Ace Step LM* variants, this may get very slow with *Memory Profiles 2 or 4* since the LM is an *Autoregressive Model*. It is why I recommed to stick to *Memory Profiles 1/3/3+* unless you have very little VRAM.
89	
90	
91	- **Kugel Audio 0**: another *TTS* with *Voice Cloning*, this one claims to outperform *ElevenLabs* !!! The nice thing about Kugel Audio is that it can be used to create Dialogues between two cloned voices. Have Fun !
92	
93	Kugel Audio is entirely an *Autoregressive Model* and quite VRAM Hungry. So either you've got 16GB VRAM and you can run it with *Memory Profile 1/3/3+* or you will have to go the slow way with other Profiles. 
94	
95	- **LTX-2 Self Refiner**: WanGP exclusive *Self Refiner* has been added to *Distilled/Non Distilled* models, so hopefully this will improve the quality of our Video Gens.
96	
97

770	
771	- LTX Video upgraded to version 0.9.8: you can now generate 1800 frames (1 min of video !) in one go without a sliding window. With the distilled model it will take only 5 minutes with a RTX 4090 (you will need 22 GB of VRAM though). I have added options to select higher humber frames if you want to experiment (go to Configuration Tab / General / Increase the Max Number of Frames, change the value and restart the App)
772	
773	- LTX Video ControlNet : it is a Control Net that allows you for instance to transfer a Human motion or Depth from a control video. It is not as powerful as Vace but can produce interesting things especially as now you can generate quickly a 1 min video. Under the scene IC-Loras (see below) for Pose, Depth and Canny are automatically loaded for you, no need to add them. 
774	
775	- LTX IC-Lora support: these are special Loras that consumes a conditional image or video
776	Beside the pose, depth and canny IC-Loras transparently loaded there is the *detailer* (https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-Video-ICLoRA-detailer-13b-0.9.8) which is basically an upsampler. Add the *detailer* as a Lora and use LTX Raw Format as control net choice to use it.
777	
778	- Matanyone is now also for the GPU Poor as its VRAM requirements have been divided by 2! (7.12 shadow update)
779	
780	- Easier way to select video resolution 
781	
782	### July 15 2025: WanGP v7.0 is an AI Powered Photoshop
783	This release turns the Wan models into Image Generators. This goes way more than allowing to generate a video made of single frame :
784	- Multiple Images generated at the same time so that you can choose the one you like best.It is Highly VRAM optimized so that you can generate for instance 4 720p Images at the same time with less than 10 GB
785	- With the *image2image* the original text2video WanGP becomes an image upsampler / restorer
786	- *Vace image2image* comes out of the box with image outpainting, person / object replacement, ...
787	- You can use in one click a newly Image generated as Start Image or Reference Image for a Video generation
788	
789	And to complete the full suite of AI Image Generators, Ladies and Gentlemen please welcome for the first time in WanGP : **Flux Kontext**.\
790	As a reminder Flux Kontext is an image editor : give it an image and a prompt and it will do the change for you.\
791	This highly optimized version of Flux Kontext will make you feel that you have been cheated all this time as WanGP Flux Kontext requires only 8 GB of VRAM to generate 4 images at the same time with no need for quantization.
792	
793	WanGP v7 comes with *Image2image* vanilla and *Vace FusinoniX*. However you can build your own finetune where you will combine a text2video or Vace model with any combination of Loras.
794	
795	Also in the news:
796	- You can now enter the *Bbox* for each speaker in *Multitalk* to precisely locate who is speaking. And to save some headaches the *Image Mask generator* will give you the *Bbox* coordinates of an area you have selected.
797	- *Film Grain* post processing to add a vintage look at your video
798	- *First Last Frame to Video* model should work much better now as I have discovered rencently its implementation was not complete
799	- More power for the finetuners, you can now embed Loras directly in the finetune definition. You can also override the default models (titles, visibility, ...) with your own finetunes. Check the doc that has been updated.
```

Critical finding — in the official LTX-2 `ICLoraPipeline`, both stages re-use the SAME `loras` at __init__ (line 78) — meaning the IC-LoRA is loaded on both stage_1 and stage_2. But the stage_2 re-uses the upscaled stage_1 latent (line 233, 260) — the context latent is preserved mid-pipeline, not re-encoded from pixels.

```
1	# LTX-2 Pipelines
2	
3	High-level pipeline implementations for generating audio-video content with Lightricks' **LTX-2** model. This package provides ready-to-use pipelines for text-to-video, image-to-video, video-to-video, and keyframe interpolation tasks.
4	
5	Pipelines are built using building blocks from [`ltx-core`](../ltx-core/) (schedulers, guiders, noisers, patchifiers) and handle the complete inference flow including model loading, encoding, decoding, and file I/O.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 📋 Overview
10	
11	LTX-2 Pipelines provides production-ready implementations that abstract away the complexity of the diffusion process, model loading, and memory management. Each pipeline is optimized for specific use cases and offers different trade-offs between speed, quality, and memory usage.
12	
13	**Key Features:**
14	
15	- 🎬 **Multiple Pipeline Types**: Text-to-video, image-to-video, video-to-video, audio-to-video, keyframe interpolation, and retake
16	- ⚡ **Optimized Performance**: Support for FP8 transformers, gradient estimation, and memory optimization
17	- 🎯 **Production Ready**: Two-stage pipelines for best quality output
18	- 🔧 **LoRA Support**: Easy integration with trained LoRA adapters
19	- 📦 **Self-Contained**: Handles model loading, encoding, decoding, and file I/O
20	- 🚀 **CLI Support**: All pipelines can be run as command-line scripts
21	
22	---
23	
24	## 🚀 Quick Start
25	
26	`ltx-pipelines` provides ready-made inference pipelines for text-to-video, image-to-video, video-to-video, audio-to-video, keyframe interpolation, and retake. Built using building blocks from [`ltx-core`](../ltx-core/), these pipelines handle the complete inference flow including model loading, encoding, decoding, and file I/O.
27	
28	## 🔧 Installation
29	
30	```bash
31	# From the repository root
32	uv sync --frozen
33	
34	# Or install as a package
35	pip install -e packages/ltx-pipelines
36	```
37	
38	### Running Pipelines
39	
40	All pipelines can be run directly from the command line. Each pipeline module is executable:
41	
42	```bash
43	# Run a pipeline (example: two-stage text-to-video)
44	python -m ltx_pipelines.ti2vid_two_stages \
45	    --checkpoint-path path/to/checkpoint.safetensors \
46	    --distilled-lora path/to/distilled_lora.safetensors 0.8 \
47	    --spatial-upsampler-path path/to/upsampler.safetensors \
48	    --gemma-root path/to/gemma \
49	    --prompt "A beautiful sunset over the ocean" \
50	    --output-path output.mp4
51	
52	# View all available options for any pipeline
53	python -m ltx_pipelines.ti2vid_two_stages --help
54	```
55	
56	Available pipeline modules:
57	
58	- `ltx_pipelines.ti2vid_two_stages` - Two-stage text/image-to-video (recommended).
59	- `ltx_pipelines.ti2vid_two_stages_hq` - Two-stage text/image-to-video (different sampler, better quality).
60	- `ltx_pipelines.ti2vid_one_stage` - Single-stage text/image-to-video.
61	- `ltx_pipelines.distilled` - Fast text/image-to-video pipeline using only the distilled model.
62	- `ltx_pipelines.ic_lora` - Video-to-video with IC-LoRA.
63	- `ltx_pipelines.keyframe_interpolation` - Keyframe interpolation.
64	- `ltx_pipelines.a2vid_two_stage` - Audio-to-video generation conditioned on an input audio.
65	- `ltx_pipelines.retake` - Regenerate a time region of an existing video.
66	
67	Use `--help` with any pipeline module to see all available options and parameters.
68	
69	---
70	
71	## 🎯 Pipeline Selection Guide
72	
73	### Quick Decision Tree
74	
75	```text
76	Do you have an existing video to modify?
77	├─ YES → Use RetakePipeline (regenerate a specific time region)
78	│
79	Do you have an audio file to drive generation?
80	├─ YES → Use A2VidPipelineTwoStage (audio-to-video)
81	│
82	Do you need to condition on existing images/videos?
83	├─ YES → Do you have reference videos for video-to-video?
84	│  ├─ YES → Use ICLoraPipeline
85	│  └─ NO → Do you have multiple keyframe images to interpolate?
86	│     ├─ YES → Use KeyframeInterpolationPipeline
87	│     └─ NO → Use TI2VidTwoStagesPipeline (image conditioning only)
88	│
89	└─ NO → Text-to-video only
90	   ├─ Do you need best quality?
91	   │  └─ YES → Use TI2VidTwoStagesPipeline (recommended for production)
92	   │
93	   └─ Do you need fastest inference?
94	      └─ YES → Use DistilledPipeline (with 8 predefined sigmas)
95	```
96	
97	> **Note:** [`TI2VidOneStagePipeline`](src/ltx_pipelines/ti2vid_one_stage.py) is primarily for educational purposes. For best quality, use two-stage pipelines ([`TI2VidTwoStagesPipeline`](src/ltx_pipelines/ti2vid_two_stages.py), [`TI2VidTwoStagesHQPipeline`](src/ltx_pipelines/ti2vid_two_stages_hq.py), [`ICLoraPipeline`](src/ltx_pipelines/ic_lora.py), [`KeyframeInterpolationPipeline`](src/ltx_pipelines/keyframe_interpolation.py), [`A2VidPipelineTwoStage`](src/ltx_pipelines/a2vid_two_stage.py), or [`DistilledPipeline`](src/ltx_pipelines/distilled.py)). For editing existing videos, use [`RetakePipeline`](src/ltx_pipelines/retake.py).
98	
99	### Features Comparison
100	
101	| Pipeline | Stages | [Multimodal Guidance](#%EF%B8%8F-multimodal-guidance) | Upsampling | Conditioning | Best For |
102	| -------- | ------ | --- | ---------- | ------------- | -------- |
103	| **TI2VidTwoStagesPipeline** | 2 | ✅ | ✅ | Image | **Production quality** (recommended) |
104	| **TI2VidTwoStagesHQPipeline** | 2 | ✅ | ✅ | Image | Same as above, res_2s sampler (higher quality) |
105	| **TI2VidOneStagePipeline** | 1 | ✅ | ❌ | Image | Educational, prototyping |
106	| **DistilledPipeline** | 2 | ❌ | ✅ | Image | Fastest inference (8 sigmas) |
107	| **ICLoraPipeline** | 2 | ✅ | ✅ | Image + Video | Video-to-video transformations |
108	| **KeyframeInterpolationPipeline** | 2 | ✅ | ✅ | Keyframes | Animation, interpolation |
109	| **A2VidPipelineTwoStage** | 2 | ✅ | ✅ | Audio + Image | Audio-driven video generation |
110	| **RetakePipeline** | 1 | ✅ | ❌ | Source Video | Regenerating a time region of a video |
111	
112	---
113	
114	## 📦 Available Pipelines
115	
116	### 1. TI2VidTwoStagesPipeline
117	
118	**Best for:** High-quality text/image-to-video generation with upsampling. **Recommended for production use.**
119	
120	**Source**: [`src/ltx_pipelines/ti2vid_two_stages.py`](src/ltx_pipelines/ti2vid_two_stages.py)
```

> AGENT

Key: In official LTX-2 ICLoraPipeline at line 87, **stage_2 uses `loras=()` — IC-LoRAs are only applied to stage_1 by design**. The upscaled stage-1 latent feeds directly into stage_2 (line 260 initial_latent), so stage_2 is a refinement pass without IC-LoRA influence. This matches our vendored Wan2GP behavior.

# Changelog
### January 1st 2026: WanGP v10.01, Happy New Year !

- **Wan 2.2 i2v Stable Vision Infinity Pro 2**: SVI Pro 2 offers potentially unlimited Videos to Continue for i2v models. It will use either the Start frame as a Reference Image or you may provide an Anchor image to be used across all the windows or multiple Anchor Images one per Window.

- **Wan 2.1 Alpha 2**: This new version of Alpha generates transparent videos with fine-grained alpha detail (hair, glow, smoke). 

- **Qwen Image 2512**: This December release offers Enhanced Human Realism, Finer Natural Details & Improved Text Rendering.

- **Wan NVP4**: *Light2xv nvfp4 support for Wan 2.1 i2v & t2v 1.3B*, you can now load nvfp4 (4 bits quantized file) in WanGP. These will make really a difference with RTX 50xx as they support natively scaled FP4 calculation. Other GPUs will get the pytorch fallback which is slower. This model can be useful for machines with low RAM but don't expect significant VRAM reduction of much faster speed for non RTX 50xx owners. You will need to install the Light2xv kernels.

- **Nunckaku int4 & fp4 support for Qwen 2509 & Z Image**: int4 versions will work with most GPUs, fp4 will accelerate only RTX50xx. You will need to install the nunchaku kernels. See lightx2v nvfp4 above, as the other comments apply here too.

- **Z Image Control Net 2.1**: Control Net upgraded should work better. I have enabled as well inpainting for the control net.

- **New Qwen Loras Accelerators Added**

*Quantization Kernels Wheels for Windows / Python 3.10 / Pytorch 2.70:*
- *Light2xv (WAN-FP4)*

# LTX + Wan2GP Big-Picture Investigation

## 1. Latest LTX version

- **Current default model**: **`ltx-2.3-22b-distilled-1.1`** (22B params, LTX-2.3 release, distilled flavor "1.1"). Weights at `Lightricks/LTX-2.3` on HF (`/tmp/ltx2-official/README.md:32-33`). The non-distilled dev sibling is `ltx-2.3-22b-dev.safetensors` (line 32).
- **User's "LTX 3 1.1"**: misremembered — there is no LTX-3. What exists is `ltx-2.3-22b-distilled-**1.1**` and `ltx-2.3-spatial-upscaler-x2-**1.1**`. LTX-2 (Oct 23 2025) is the new foundation model line that supersedes LTX-Video 0.9.x. LTX-2.3 is the current HF variant (`/tmp/ltx2-official/README.md:29`). The old `ltxv-13b-0.9.8-distilled` repo (`/tmp/ltx-official/`) is archived and now just a redirect notice to LTX-2 (last commit `4b2d053 Merge pull request #261 ... ltx2-redirect-notice`).
- **What's new vs ltxv-13b-0.9.8-distilled**: synchronized audio+video (`/tmp/ltx2-official/README.md:9`); 22B transformer (up from 13B); new Gemma-3-12b text encoder; new VAE, vocoder, audio VAE; `res_2s` second-order sampler (`TI2VidTwoStagesHQPipeline`); spatial+temporal upscalers at 1.1; 8-sigma DistilledPipeline; audio-to-video (`A2VidPipelineTwoStage`); `RetakePipeline` (regenerate a time region); `KeyframeInterpolationPipeline`.
- **IC-LoRA variants shipped** (`/tmp/ltx2-official/README.md:49-59`): `LTX-2.3-22b-IC-LoRA-Union-Control` (combined pose/depth/canny, ref downscale 0.5), `LTX-2.3-22b-IC-LoRA-Motion-Track-Control`, `LTX-2-19b-IC-LoRA-Detailer`, `LTX-2-19b-IC-LoRA-Pose-Control`, plus seven 19B Camera-Control LoRAs (Dolly In/Left/Out/Right, Jib Down/Up, Static).
- **Latest pipeline/conditioning changes**: `ICLoraPipeline` in LTX-2 loads IC-LoRA on **stage 1 only** (`/tmp/ltx2-official/packages/ltx-pipelines/src/ltx_pipelines/ic_lora.py:78` `loras=tuple(loras)` vs `:87` `loras=()`). `video_conditioning` is a list of `(path, strength)` tuples (line 122). LoRA metadata now stores `reference_downscale_factor` read at init (lines 98–111). Stage 2 uses the upscaled stage-1 **latent** as `initial_latent` (line 260) — no pixel round-trip between stages.
- **New upscale / detailer workflow**: LTX-2 has native `VideoUpsampler` used by every two-stage pipeline; Lightricks ships the Detailer only as a **19B IC-LoRA** (no 22B/2.3 detailer yet). Old 0.9.8 detailer (`LTX-Video-ICLoRA-detailer-13b-0.9.8`) is only documented via ComfyUI workflow `ltxv-13b-upscale.json` (`/tmp/ltx-official/README.md:109-110`) — not in the pipeline API.

## 2. deepbeepmeep/Wan2GP upstream

- **IC-LoRA auto-injection**: `/tmp/wan2gp-official/models/ltx2/ltx2.py:783-832` `get_loras_transformer()`. For `ltx2_22B` distilled, when any `P`/`D`/`E` char is in `video_prompt_type`, it pulls a single `"union-control"` preload URL (line 826 `_append_preload_lora("union-control", 1.0)`). For the 19B it switches per-mode (lines 749-755). For non-distilled + guidance_phases>1 it injects `"distilled-lora"` as a stage-multiplier LoRA (line 823).
- **Mode→LoRA registry location**: two layers.
  1. Model-level `preload_URLs` in `/tmp/wan2gp-official/defaults/ltx2_22B_distilled_1_1.json:10-13` (hardcodes the `ic-lora-union-control-ref0.5` + `ic-lora-outpaint` URLs).
  2. Arch spec dict in `/tmp/wan2gp-official/models/ltx2/ltx2_handler.py:17-57` (`union_control_lora`, `outpaint_lora`, `distilled_1_1_lora` keys).
  — There is **no Python dict mapping `"pose"/"depth"/"canny" → specific LoRA file`** like our `_IC_LORA_BY_MODE` (`reigh-worker/source/core/params/travel_guidance.py:32`). Upstream relies on a single union LoRA + substring matching (`"union-control" in file_name`).
- **Detailer support for LTX-2**: **no**. Grep for `detailer` across `/tmp/wan2gp-official/models/ltx2` returns zero hits. The only detailer mention in the whole repo is the legacy 0.9.8 ComfyUI workflow in `docs/CHANGELOG.md:776` ("Add the *detailer* as a Lora and use LTX Raw Format as control net choice"). LTX-2 has `self_refiner` (`/tmp/wan2gp-official/shared/utils/self_refiner.py` + `/tmp/wan2gp-official/models/ltx2/ltx2_handler.py:227-228` `"self_refiner": True`) which is a different mechanism (PnP/perturbation-based intra-denoise self-refinement) that WanGP added Feb 4 2026.
- **Stage-2 LoRA handling**: upstream has `skip_stage_2` (`/tmp/wan2gp-official/models/ltx2/ltx2.py:1159` `skip_stage_2 = guide_phases <=1`), and at line 918 **auto-forces `guide_phases = 1` whenever P/D/E/V appears in `video_prompt_type`** — i.e., upstream completely skips stage 2 when IC-LoRA conditioning is active. For plain two-stage (non-IC-LoRA), `TI2VidTwoStagesPipeline` swaps in the `distilled_lora` on stage_2 only (`/tmp/wan2gp-official/models/ltx2/ltx_pipelines/ti2vid_two_stages.py:93-96`) — stage_2 never runs IC-LoRA.
- **Preprocessor choices** (`/tmp/wan2gp-official/preprocessing/`): `dwpose/` (ONNX pose), `depth_anything_v2/`, `midas/`, `canny.py`, `scribble.py`, `gray.py`, `flow.py`, `raft/`, `matanyone/`, `arc/face_encoder.py`. Same DWPose + Depth Anything V2 + Canny as ours, plus extras (MiDaS, Matanyone segmentation, RAFT flow, face embedding) we don't wire up.
- **Downscale factor knob**: yes, `_infer_ic_lora_downscale_factor` at `/tmp/wan2gp-official/models/ltx2/ltx2.py:430-447` parses `-ref0.5` style suffixes from LoRA filename (not from metadata). Upstream returns `min(factors)`; vendored version raises on conflict (`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-worker/Wan2GP/models/ltx2/ltx2.py:442-445`).
- **Latest LTX version handling**: upstream has `ltx2_22B_1_1.json` + `ltx2_22B_distilled_1_1.json` defaults and `distilled_1_1_lora` key in arch spec (`ltx2_handler.py:43`). Our vendored copy does not.
- **Our vendored copy staleness**: no `.git` dir (confirmed `ls -la …/Wan2GP/.git` → no such file). CHANGELOG version headers: vendored top entry **Jan 1 2026 / v10.01** (`…/Wan2GP/docs/CHANGELOG.md:2`); upstream top **Feb 19 2026 / v10.951** (`/tmp/wan2gp-official/docs/CHANGELOG.md:2`) — ~50 days and ~9 minor releases behind. 22 files differ in `models/ltx2/` alone (4303 diff lines). Major missing since fork: LTX-2 Self-Refiner (Feb 4), res2s HQ sampler (`models/ltx2/ltx_pipelines/utils/res2s.py` — file doesn't exist vendored), prompt_enhancer.py (missing vendored), LTX-2.3 distilled 1.1 + nvfp4 defaults, outpaint IC-LoRA + gamma preprocessing (`_apply_gamma_to_media`, `LTX2_OUTPAINT_GAMMA`, `LTX2_DISABLE_STAGE2_WITH_CONTROL_VIDEO` constants lines 46-50 upstream — all absent vendored), plus Index TTS 2 / Ace Step / Kugel Audio (not LTX-relevant).

## 3. Detailer placement

- **LTX official guidance**: Lightricks ships the LTX-2 Detailer **only as an IC-LoRA** (`LTX-2-19b-IC-LoRA-Detailer`, `/tmp/ltx2-official/README.md:51`) — used via `ICLoraPipeline` with the detailer file passed in `loras=[…]`. By pipeline design, IC-LoRAs run **stage-1 only** (file:line above). There is no post-decode detail pipeline; detail happens during denoise of the upscaled latent (stage_2 `initial_latent=upscaled_video_latent`, `ic_lora.py:260`). For 0.9.8 the old pattern was ComfyUI workflow `ltxv-13b-upscale.json` — a second full LTX call on decoded video using "LTX Raw Format" conditioning (CHANGELOG.md:776). So: LTX community has historically done **post-gen pixel-in detailer as a second LTX inference call** (not latent chaining).
- **Wan2GP upstream guidance**: no detailer integration for LTX-2. For LTX 0.9.8 only, `docs/CHANGELOG.md:776` tells users to "Add the detailer as a Lora and use LTX Raw Format as control net choice" — a user-driven pixel-level re-inference, not inline. Upstream's own quality pass is `self_refiner` (PnP during denoise, `/tmp/wan2gp-official/models/ltx2/ltx2_handler.py:413`) — not a detailer.
- **Technical blockers to post-gen**: none that I can find. The LTX-2 Detailer is a standard IC-LoRA over a `video_conditioning=[(video_path, strength)]` signature (`ic_lora.py:122, 274`), which takes a decoded video as input. Nothing in the LoRA interface requires mid-sample latents. The stage_2 latent-sharing in `ICLoraPipeline` is an **efficiency** choice (skip VAE encode/decode), not a correctness requirement. Quality concern is real (reported round-trip softening), but functionally viable.
- **Existing reigh-worker post-gen hooks we could reuse**:
  - `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-worker/source/task_handlers/rife_interpolate.py:1-30` — already a clean post-gen task handler pattern (reads a produced file, runs ops, writes new file, registers in DB).
  - `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-worker/source/media/video/hires_utils.py:1-70` — "two-pass hires fix" abstraction across Qwen/Z-Image/Flux with `parse_config(scale, steps, denoise, upscale_method)` and `upscale_latents` — same shape as what an LTX detailer pass needs; currently LTX-free but extensible.
  - `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-worker/source/task_handlers/edit_video_orchestrator.py` + `magic_edit.py` — already decouple "orchestrator builds payload → second gen call". `edit_video_orchestrator.py` already threads `enhance_prompt` through VLM (line 582-611).
  - `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-worker/Wan2GP/postprocessing/` contains `film_grain.py`, `mmaudio`, `rife` — the postprocessing slot exists for a new `ltx_detailer.py` sibling.

## Bottom line

"Making deepbeepmeep's approach our default" is mostly a **re-sync plus a deletion**: (1) refresh the vendored Wan2GP tree (~50 days / 22 files behind in `models/ltx2/` alone, missing res2s, self-refiner, outpaint-LoRA gamma, LTX-2.3 1.1 defaults, prompt_enhancer.py) or stop vendoring and depend on a pinned upstream; (2) collapse our `_IC_LORA_BY_MODE` mode-split to the single union-control LoRA for 22B like upstream does at `ltx2.py:826`, since 2.3-22B has no per-mode LoRAs beyond cameraman and the union LoRA handles P/D/E. The meaningful code change is tiny — our registry in `travel_guidance.py:32-37` already falls back to union, so we could just delete the mode-split branch on non-cameraman modes.

Post-gen detailing is **safe in principle but never officially recommended for LTX-2** — Lightricks ships the detailer as an IC-LoRA, and both ICLoraPipeline (stage-1-only LoRA + stage-2 latent chaining) and upstream's `self_refiner` avoid the VAE round-trip specifically for quality. The community's 0.9.8 pattern (second full LTX call on decoded video with the detailer LoRA) is the only documented post-gen recipe and has the known softening cost. Minimum-risk path: add an optional `ltx_detailer` post-processing handler modeled on `rife_interpolate.py` that wraps `ICLoraPipeline` with the 19B detailer LoRA — gated off by default, decoupled from the main denoise, and cheap to A/B against inline.

## 1. Role & Mission
Drive the megaplan metaplan workflow through the CLI until the document artifact is written or a defined breakpoint requires the outer conversation.

Always follow these priorities:
1. Latest user direction via notes or resume messages.
2. Live CLI state from `megaplan status --plan <name>`.
3. Workflow rules in this template.

Rules: operate via `megaplan` CLI only, no direct worker calls. Keep the outer conversation clean. Follow `orchestrator_guidance` after `gate` unless you have concrete reason to disagree.

## 2. Startup
1. `raw_config.execution.auto_approve` is explicitly set — AUTO_APPROVE_FLAG expands to empty string.
2. `raw_config.execution.robustness` is NOT explicitly set — ROBUSTNESS_FLAG expands to `--robustness standard`.
3. Run: `megaplan init --project-dir [REDACTED] --robustness standard --mode metaplan --output docs/WAN2GP_FORK_MIGRATION_PLAN.md "<IDEA>"` where `<IDEA>` is the full idea text above.
4. Capture plan name. Output `PLAN_NAME: <name>` on its own line before any BREAKPOINT/COMPLETE.
5. Run `megaplan status --plan <name>`.

## 3. Phase Routing — Standard Robustness (metaplan mode)
Loop: `init → prep → plan → critique → gate → (revise | finalize) → execute → review`

Gate decision tree:
- `gate_unset` (critiqued, valid_next has `gate`): run gate.
- `gate_iterate` (recommendation=ITERATE): run revise, then critique, then gate.
- `gate_escalate` (recommendation=ESCALATE): stop with BREAKPOINT: GATE_ESCALATE.
- `gate_proceed_blocked` (recommendation=PROCEED but preflight blocked): use `orchestrator_guidance` + `preflight_results` to fix via revise. If unresolvable without user input, BREAKPOINT: GATE_BLOCKED.
- `gate_proceed` (recommendation=PROCEED and preflight passed, state=gated): run finalize.

After execute in metaplan mode, the artifact is the written document. Review will judge section delivery rather than code. If review returns `needs_rework`, run execute again from finalized. Cap is 3 rework cycles before CLI force-proceeds.

## 4. After Every Phase
Immediately run `megaplan status --plan <name>`. Re-read `state`, `next_step`, `valid_next`. If `notes_count > 0`, read full notes array. If phase response and status disagree, trust status.

## 5. Breakpoints
Format:
BREAKPOINT: <type>
Plan: <name>
State: <state>
Summary: <short reason>
Context: <artifacts or decision needed>

Types for standard metaplan:
- GATE_ESCALATE
- GATE_BLOCKED
- PHASE_ESCALATE (non-execute phase fails after retry)
- EXECUTE_ESCALATE (execute no-progress cap or repeated blockers)

No EXECUTE_APPROVAL needed — auto-approve is on.

## 6. Safeguards
Non-execute: retry once with `--fresh` on failure or unusable output; BREAKPOINT: PHASE_ESCALATE after that.
Execute: 3 consecutive attempts without forward progress → BREAKPOINT: EXECUTE_ESCALATE.
Review `needs_rework` is a normal branch, not a failure — run execute again.

## 7. Resume Protocol
On resume: run `megaplan status`, read full `notes`, resume from current CLI state and `next_step`, not memory.

## 8. Execution
- After gated, run `megaplan finalize --plan <name>`.
- Auto-approve: run `megaplan execute --plan <name> --confirm-destructive`.
- Per-batch if indicated: use `megaplan progress` between batches; re-run same batch N after timeout.

## 9. Overrides
`override add-note` safe any active state. `override force-proceed` from `critiqued` → `gated`. `override replan` from `critiqued`/`gated`/`finalized` — read latest plan file, edit directly, continue with `critique`.

## 10. Completion Format
COMPLETE: megaplan run finished
Plan: <name>
Final state: <state>
Summary: <outcome — document written, sprint count, key decisions>
Artifacts: docs/WAN2GP_FORK_MIGRATION_PLAN.md path, any additional outputs
Follow-up: <if anything remains>

Be concise. Only narrate phase transitions and final result.

267	  "signals": {
268	    "iteration": 3,
269	    "idea": "Produce a design document that plans the full migration of reigh-worker's vendored deepbeepmeep/Wan2GP code from its current drifted snapshot (~50 days / ~9 minor versions behind, no .git directory) into a maintainable fork-plus-patch-layer relationship, broken into 2-week sprints. The document's job is to define the sprints, not to execute them.\n\nNon-negotiable constraint throughout every sprint: NO FUNCTIONALITY MAY BE LOST. Every behavior reigh-worker currently depends on \u2014 IC-LoRA auto-injection for pose/depth/canny/cameraman modes (source/core/params/travel_guidance.py _IC_LORA_BY_MODE, _auto_inject_travel_guidance_lora), the newly-landed ltx_anchor travel guidance kind, the existing ltx_control and ltx_hybrid travel paths, the vendored ICLoraPipeline behavior, the custom patches our vendored tree carries \u2014 must survive, be explicitly accounted for in the sprint plan, and have a verification step.\n\nContext the document must incorporate (treat as authoritative background):\n\n- Current situation: reigh-worker/Wan2GP/ is a flat copy without a .git directory. Cannot be rebased. Upstream is deepbeepmeep/Wan2GP. Approximately 50 days behind (vendored top changelog entry is v10.01 / 2026-01-01; upstream top is v10.951 / 2026-02-19). 22 files differ in Wan2GP/models/ltx2/ alone, ~4303 diff lines.\n- Missing upstream features we want: ltx2_22B_distilled_1_1.json defaults, shared/utils/self_refiner.py (Feb 4), models/ltx2/ltx_pipelines/utils/res2s.py (res_2s sampler), outpaint IC-LoRA + gamma preprocessing (_apply_gamma_to_media, LTX2_OUTPAINT_GAMMA, LTX2_DISABLE_STAGE2_WITH_CONTROL_VIDEO constants), prompt_enhancer improvements.\n- Upstream's IC-LoRA pattern is simpler than ours: single union-control preload URL for distilled 22B (models/ltx2/ltx2.py:783-832), substring-matched, no per-mode Python dict like our _IC_LORA_BY_MODE. Upstream auto-forces guide_phases=1 when P/D/E in video_prompt_type (ltx2.py:918). Cameraman-style per-mode LoRAs are 19B (not 22B). This means a large chunk of our custom IC-LoRA registry logic is either convergeable to upstream's approach or should become a thin override.\n- Detailer situation: LTX-2 detailer is 19B only (no 22B/2.3 variant exists). Lightricks' ICLoraPipeline runs LoRA stage-1-only with stage-2 latent chaining. Upstream has no LTX-2 detailer integration. self_refiner (PnP mid-denoise) is the nearest thing upstream offers and is likely to obviate inline detailing after we adopt it.\n- User preference: detailer, if we build it, should be a post-gen task handler (like source/task_handlers/rife_interpolate.py) rather than inline in the travel pipeline. This is independent of the fork migration but is a natural follow-up sprint.\n- Constraint inventory (what reigh-worker currently depends on that must survive):\n  - IC-LoRA auto-injection by mode (source/task_handlers/tasks/task_registry.py:955-987) wiring union-control to pose/depth/canny and cameraman LoRA to cameraman mode.\n  - Pixel cross-fade guide video path for ltx_control (source/media/video/travel_guide.py) \u2014 must NOT be broken by the resync even though it's arguably legacy.\n  - ltx_anchor kind just shipped in commit 9656cc90 \u2014 must survive the resync. The rename _build_segment_hybrid_guidance_config \u2192 _build_segment_anchor_guidance_config touched vendored tests indirectly; verify.\n  - The vendored Wan2GP/models/ltx2/ltx_core/tools.py:66-79 clear_conditioning that strips appended keyframe tokens before VAE decode \u2014 load-bearing for ltx_anchor, must not be accidentally reverted to an upstream version lacking it if we have patches here.\n  - IC-LoRA dedup logic (task_registry.py:961-968).\n  - Travel orchestrator PATH A skip for ltx_anchor (orchestrator.py:1278-1289) and _build_segment_anchor_guidance_config rename (orchestrator.py).\n  - Existing test suite: tests/test_travel_guidance_config.py (20 ltx_anchor tests), tests/test_travel_ltx_vpt.py (8 runtime tests incl. source tripwire), tests/test_ltx_hybrid_travel.py (23 tests, recently promoted to tracked via .gitignore allowlist), tests/test_ltx_hybrid_vgkfi.py, tests/test_travel_payload_contracts.py, tests/test_travel_orchestrator_terminal_gating.py.\n\nOpen design decisions the document must resolve (as Settled Decisions with rationale):\n\n1. Fork shape: submodule pinned to upstream SHA vs. our own long-running fork on GitHub (e.g. banodoco/Wan2GP) vs. monkeypatch-only with upstream as a dep. Probably a hybrid \u2014 fork + minimal monkeypatch layer for things that shouldn't be in the fork. Document must pick one concretely.\n2. Patch triage buckets: every deviation between our vendored tree and upstream gets classified as (a) accept upstream \u2014 stale not intentional, (b) upstreamable \u2014 PR to deepbeepmeep, (c) banodoco-specific \u2014 carry in fork or as override, (d) cruft \u2014 drop. Document must define the triage process as a sprint task.\n3. Initial resync cadence: do we cut over to upstream head all at once, or stage by subsystem (e.g., models/ltx2/ first, then shared/, then postprocessing/)? Document must pick.\n4. LTX 2.3 distilled 1.1 default promotion: bundle into the migration, or hold for a separate A/B sprint? Document must pick.\n5. res_2s / self_refiner exposure: off-by-default flags, or promote to default once upstream does? Document must pick.\n6. Post-gen detailer sprint inclusion: does this sit inside the fork migration sprint plan (as a sprint 3 or 4), or is it a separate initiative? Document must pick.\n7. Rebase cadence post-migration: weekly? Monthly? Triggered by specific upstream events? Document must pick.\n8. CI / drift detection: how do we avoid re-drifting once we're synced? Document must propose a specific mechanism (scheduled CI job comparing to upstream head, etc.).\n\nTarget shape of the final document:\n- Executive summary (what, why, how long, what we're protecting)\n- Current-state inventory (what's vendored, what's drifted, what's load-bearing)\n- Fork architecture decision (the Settled Decisions on shape, patch triage, cadence)\n- Sprint breakdown: 3-5 sprints of 2 weeks each, each with: goals, deliverables, verification gates, rollback plan, explicit functionality-preservation checks. First sprint should be inventory-heavy (the diff triage is where the risk lives). Last sprint should cover sustainability (rebase cadence, CI, detection).\n- Risk register: what could go wrong per sprint, probability, impact, mitigation\n- Success criteria: objective checks for migration complete vs migration in progress vs regression observed\n- Explicit Settled Decisions section using the canonical megaplan format (id: SD-NNN, load_bearing, decision, rationale)\n\nOut of scope (document should note these explicitly as non-goals): flipping ltx_anchor to default, real-GPU empirical validation of the new defaults, upscaler-pass anchor re-injection, identity-drift fixes.\n\nHonor the memory-note constraint: do NOT include hard-halt prerequisite clauses of the form halt when MX not shipped. Each sprint must be able to proceed, revise scope, or explicitly deprioritize \u2014 but not sit in force-proceed limbo.",

## 2. Startup

## 3. Phase Routing — Light Robustness

If per-batch execute is indicated, drive each batch sequentially with `--batch N` starting from 1; call `megaplan progress` between batches.

## 4. After Every Phase
Immediately run `megaplan status --plan <name>`. Re-read state/next_step/valid_next. Read all notes if notes_count>0. Trust status over phase-response when they disagree.

## 5. Breakpoints
Only use a breakpoint for these cases. Format:
BREAKPOINT: <type>
Plan: <name>
State: <state>
Summary: <short reason>
Context: <what user needs to decide>

Applicable types:
- PHASE_ESCALATE: non-execute phase fails after one `--fresh` retry.
- EXECUTE_ESCALATE: 3 consecutive execute attempts without forward progress.
- GH_AUTH_FAIL: if the gh fork operation fails for auth/permission reasons AND the fallback to user namespace is also denied. Surface with concrete error message and let user choose org.

## 6. Safeguards
Non-execute: retry once with `--fresh` on failure. If same error twice → BREAKPOINT: PHASE_ESCALATE.
Execute: 3 consecutive attempts without forward progress (tasks_done not advancing) → BREAKPOINT: EXECUTE_ESCALATE.
Per-batch execute: re-run same `--batch N` if it times out; the harness merges untracked tasks.

## 7. Waiting
When active_step.recommended_action == "wait" and health == "healthy", wait via a blocking Bash call: `sleep <recommended_next_check_seconds>` then re-run `megaplan status`. Do NOT use run_in_background on the sleep — you must block until the phase advances or the sleep completes.

Cap monitoring at 90 minutes wall-clock. If not terminal by then → BREAKPOINT: EXECUTE_ESCALATE.

## 8. Completion Format
COMPLETE: megaplan run finished
Plan: <plan-name>
Final state: <state>
Summary: Sprint 1 of Wan2GP fork migration. Fork created at <banodoco/Wan2GP or fallback>. Triage CSV has <N> rows covering <M> differing files, including clear_conditioning pre-classified as bucket (c). Baseline tag wan2gp-mig-sprint-1-baseline recorded.
Artifacts: docs/wan2gp-triage.csv, git tag wan2gp-mig-sprint-1-baseline, fork URL
Follow-up: Sprint 2 ready to launch.

## 9. Hard rules
- Do NOT modify any files under reigh-worker/source/ or reigh-worker/Wan2GP/.
- Do NOT commit. The user reviews the diff and commits.
- Do NOT invoke megaplan skill or nested megaplan CLI commands — this IS the megaplan runner.
- Do NOT read previous subagent transcripts.

Start now.

## 1. Role & Mission
Drive the megaplan code-mode workflow via the CLI until the run reaches terminal state or a defined breakpoint. Use `--from-doc docs/WAN2GP_FORK_MIGRATION_PLAN.md` so the planner inherits the 8 Settled Decisions as success criteria (load_bearing=true → must; load_bearing=false → info).

Priorities: (1) user notes, (2) live CLI state, (3) this template, (4) your memory.

Rules: use the megaplan CLI only; do not run the workflow manually outside it; follow `orchestrator_guidance` after gate unless you have concrete evidence against it from plan artifacts.

## 2. Startup
1. AUTO_APPROVE_FLAG expands to empty string (auto_approve is explicitly true in raw_config).
2. ROBUSTNESS_FLAG expands to `--robustness standard` (robustness NOT set in raw_config).
3. Run: `megaplan init --project-dir [REDACTED] --robustness standard --from-doc docs/WAN2GP_FORK_MIGRATION_PLAN.md "<IDEA>"` where `<IDEA>` is the full idea text above.
4. Capture plan name. Output `PLAN_NAME: <name>` on its own line before any BREAKPOINT/COMPLETE.
5. Run `megaplan status --plan <name>`.

## 3. Phase Routing — Standard
Standard loop: `init → prep → plan → critique → gate → (revise | finalize) → execute → review`.

Gate decision tree:
- PROCEED + preflight passed (state=gated): run `finalize`.
- PROCEED + preflight blocked (state=critiqued, valid_next includes revise + override force-proceed): use `orchestrator_guidance` + `preflight_results` to fix via revise. If unresolvable → BREAKPOINT: GATE_BLOCKED.
- ITERATE (valid_next has revise): run `revise`, back to critique, back to gate.
- ESCALATE: BREAKPOINT: GATE_ESCALATE.

After gated → finalize → execute. After execute, run review. Review `needs_rework` is normal — CLI rewinds to finalized; re-run execute; cap 3 rework cycles.

Per-batch execute: if the execution briefing indicates batching, drive each `--batch N` sequentially, polling `megaplan progress` between.

## 4. After Every Phase
Run `megaplan status --plan <name>` immediately after each phase. Re-read state/next_step/valid_next. Read all notes if notes_count>0. Trust status over phase-response.

## 5. Breakpoints
Format:
BREAKPOINT: <type>
Plan: <name>
State: <state>
Summary: <short reason>
Context: <what user needs to decide>

Types in scope for standard:
- GATE_ESCALATE: gate recommendation ESCALATE.
- GATE_BLOCKED: PROCEED but preflight blocked and not resolvable via revise.
- PHASE_ESCALATE: non-execute phase fails twice (one `--fresh` retry consumed).
- EXECUTE_ESCALATE: 3 consecutive execute attempts without forward progress.
- SUBMODULE_BLOCKER: submodule cut-over hits a git-level blocker (existing .gitmodules conflict, uncommitted changes in Wan2GP/, submodule init fails). Surface concrete error + let user decide rollback vs force.

## 6. Safeguards
Non-execute: retry once with `--fresh` on failure. Same error twice → BREAKPOINT: PHASE_ESCALATE.
Execute: 3 consecutive no-progress attempts → BREAKPOINT: EXECUTE_ESCALATE. Per-batch timeouts: re-run same `--batch N`; harness reconciles.
Review `needs_rework`: normal loop, re-run execute.

## 7. Waiting
When active_step.recommended_action=="wait" and health=="healthy", block via `sleep <recommended_next_check_seconds>` in a single Bash call. Do NOT run_in_background the sleep — it must block this agent until the phase advances.

Cap total monitoring at 120 minutes wall-clock. Not terminal by then → BREAKPOINT: EXECUTE_ESCALATE.

## 8. Completion Format
COMPLETE: megaplan run finished
Plan: <name>
Final state: <state>
Summary: Sprint 2 cut-over complete. Submodule mounted at reigh-worker/Wan2GP/ pointing at banodoco/Wan2GP commit <SHA>. shared/ + postprocessing/ resynced. self_refiner aligned. res2s.py added behind flag. Stale docs updated in <file list>. Path-contract smoke green. 6-file travel suite: <N>/<M> pass. Doc sweep: zero hits. Baseline tag wan2gp-mig-sprint-2-baseline recorded.
Artifacts: .gitmodules, submodule at Wan2GP/, updated README.md/STRUCTURE.md/docs/KIJAI_SVI_IMPLEMENTATION.md, git tag wan2gp-mig-sprint-2-baseline
Follow-up: Sprint 3 ready to launch (hot-zone models/ltx2/ resync + new IC-LoRA tests).

## 9. Hard rules
- Do NOT touch any files under `Wan2GP/models/ltx2/` in Sprint 2. That's Sprint 3.
- Do NOT change behavior. Only relocation (flat→submodule) + low-risk drift alignment + doc updates.
- Do NOT commit final work. Leave changes staged for user review.
- Do NOT invoke megaplan skill or nested megaplan runs.
- Do NOT read previous subagent transcripts.
- Do NOT flip any default (res_2s off, distilled 1.1 off, self_refiner off-by-default per SD-005).

## Phase routing — standard

Gate decision tree (after re-critique):
- PROCEED + preflight passed (state=gated): run `finalize`.
- PROCEED + preflight blocked: use `orchestrator_guidance` + `preflight_results` to fix via revise. If unresolvable → BREAKPOINT: GATE_BLOCKED.
- ITERATE (valid_next has revise): run revise, back to critique, back to gate. Cap: if we get to iteration 6 without PROCEED, BREAKPOINT: GATE_ESCALATE (too many iterations is its own signal).
- ESCALATE: BREAKPOINT: GATE_ESCALATE.

After `gated`: finalize → execute → review. If review `needs_rework`, re-run execute (normal rework loop; CLI caps at 3 cycles).

Per-batch execute: if indicated, drive each `--batch N` sequentially, polling `megaplan progress` between.

## After every phase

When active_step.recommended_action=="wait" and health=="healthy", block via `sleep <recommended_next_check_seconds>` in a single Bash call (NOT run_in_background — must block this agent).

Format:
BREAKPOINT: <type>
Plan: execute-sprint-2-of-the-20260421-2202
State: <state>
Summary: <short reason>

Types:
- GATE_ESCALATE: gate recommendation ESCALATE OR iteration 6 reached without PROCEED.
- GATE_BLOCKED: PROCEED but preflight blocked and not resolvable.
- PHASE_ESCALATE: non-execute phase fails twice (one `--fresh` consumed).
- EXECUTE_ESCALATE: 3 consecutive execute attempts without forward progress.
- SUBMODULE_BLOCKER: git-level blocker on submodule conversion (.gitmodules conflict, uncommitted changes in Wan2GP/, submodule init fail).

- Do not skip required phases for the selected robustness level.
- Do not emit a breakpoint unless one of the breakpoint rules below says to.

## 2. Startup
1. Run `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/megaplan/.venv/bin/python -m megaplan init --project-dir [REDACTED] --from-doc docs/WAN2GP_FORK_MIGRATION_PLAN.md "<the Idea above, verbatim>"`. Config has auto_approve=true and robustness=standard as explicit overrides, so omit --auto-approve and --robustness flags.
2. Capture the returned plan name.
3. Output `PLAN_NAME: <name>` on its own line immediately after init and before any `BREAKPOINT:` or `COMPLETE:`.
4. Run `megaplan status --plan <name>` and use that plan name for every subsequent command.

## 3. Phase Routing (standard robustness)
`init -> prep -> plan -> critique -> gate -> [revise if needed] -> finalize -> execute -> review`

After each phase, read `state`, `next_step`, `valid_next`, and `notes` (read full array if `notes_count > 0`). Follow `orchestrator_guidance` after gate unless you have concrete counter-evidence.

For execution with many batches, use per-batch mode:
```
megaplan execute --plan <name> --confirm-destructive --user-approved --batch 1
megaplan execute --plan <name> --confirm-destructive --user-approved --batch 2
...
```
Check `megaplan progress --plan <name>` between batches. On timeout or stall, re-run the same `--batch N`; the harness reconciles untracked tasks.

## 4. Breakpoint Rules
Emit `BREAKPOINT: <short-reason>\n<details>` and stop ONLY for:
- GATE_ESCALATE: gate returns escalate/block and orchestrator_guidance says human judgment needed
- REVIEW_NEEDS_REWORK: review rejects a must-criterion
- SUBMODULE_PUSH: executor needs to push to banodoco/Wan2GP reigh-sprint-3 — orchestrator will do it; post the branch name and commit SHA
- SUBMODULE_WRITE_BLOCKED: executor needs .git/ index writes — orchestrator will do it
- DESTRUCTIVE_OP_REQUEST: force-push, branch delete, git reset --hard, DB ops, squash-merge to main
- UNRESOLVABLE_CONFLICT: merge conflict the executor cannot resolve

Do NOT breakpoint for: non-destructive public actions (branch creation on fork, PR creation, issues, tags). The user has standing autonomous authorization for those during this migration — do them yourself via the orchestrator if the executor sandbox blocks them, or resume directly.

## 5. Completion
When the plan reaches terminal state (done, aborted, failed):
- Read the final review artifact if available
- Emit `COMPLETE: megaplan run finished\nPlan: <name>\nFinal state: <state>\nSummary: <2-3 sentence summary>\nArtifacts: <key file paths>\nFollow-up: <any handoff to next sprint or user action required>`

Start now with the init call. Remember: do not commit reigh-worker changes — leave staged.

## Sandbox rules (learned from Sprints 1–2)
- Executor (codex) CANNOT write to `.git/` or push to remotes. The outer orchestrator handles submodule commits/pushes and feeds results via `megaplan override add-note`.
- `uv sync` fails on darwin-arm64 (decord==0.6.0 wheel gap). Sprint 2 built a minimal smoke venv at `/tmp/sprint2-smoke-venv`. You may reuse it (check if it still exists) or build `/tmp/sprint3-smoke-venv` with the same packages: gradio torch diffusers transformers mmgp scipy Pillow numpy torchvision opencv-python imageio rembg onnxruntime ffmpeg-python
- Do NOT commit final reigh-worker work. Leave reigh-worker changes staged for user review (same rule as Sprint 2).

## Startup sequence
1. Run `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/megaplan/.venv/bin/python -m megaplan status --plan execute-sprint-3-of-the-20260422-0132` to confirm state.
2. Output `PLAN_NAME: execute-sprint-3-of-the-20260422-0132` on its own line.
3. If state is `finalized`, run `megaplan execute --plan execute-sprint-3-of-the-20260422-0132 --confirm-destructive --user-approved`. For long runs, prefer per-batch:
   `megaplan execute --plan <name> --confirm-destructive --user-approved --batch N`
   Between batches poll `megaplan progress --plan <name>`.
4. After execute reaches `executed`, run `megaplan review --plan <name>`.
5. If review returns `needs_rework`, follow the CLI's `next_step` routing (finalize → execute again).

## Breakpoint conditions (emit `BREAKPOINT: <reason>\n<details>` and stop ONLY for these)
- GATE_ESCALATE: gate returns escalate/block and orchestrator_guidance says human judgment needed (n/a — past gate)
- REVIEW_NEEDS_REWORK: review rejects a must-criterion and replan is needed
- SUBMODULE_PUSH: executor needs to push to `banodoco/Wan2GP reigh-sprint-3` — post branch name + commit SHA, orchestrator will push
- SUBMODULE_WRITE_BLOCKED: executor needs `.git/` index writes — orchestrator will do it
- DESTRUCTIVE_OP_REQUEST: force-push, branch delete, `git reset --hard`, DB ops, squash-merge to main
- UNRESOLVABLE_CONFLICT: merge conflict the executor cannot resolve
- EXECUTE_STALLED: execute step hung or returned the same batch as pending after retry

Do NOT breakpoint for: non-destructive public actions (branch creation on fork, PR creation, issues, tags). User has standing autonomous authorization during this migration.

CLEAR_CONDITIONING_LINES_66_79:
    def clear_conditioning(self, latent_state: LatentState) -> LatentState:
        """
        Clear the conditioning from the latent state. This method removes extra tokens from the end of the latent.
        Therefore, conditioning items should add extra tokens ONLY to the end of the latent.
        """
        latent_state = latent_state.clone()

        num_tokens = self.patchifier.get_token_count(self.target_shape)
        latent = latent_state.latent[:, :num_tokens]
        clean_latent = latent_state.clean_latent[:, :num_tokens]
        denoise_mask = torch.ones_like(latent_state.denoise_mask)[:, :num_tokens]
        positions = latent_state.positions[:, :, :num_tokens]

        return LatentState(latent=latent, denoise_mask=denoise_mask, positions=positions, clean_latent=clean_latent)
```

def get_custom_prompt_enhancer_instructions(model_type, prompt_enhancer_mode, is_image, enhancer_kwargs):
    audio_prompt_type =enhancer_kwargs.get("audio_prompt_type", "")
    any_source_image = "I" in prompt_enhancer_mode
    if "A" in audio_prompt_type and "1" in audio_prompt_type:
        ID_LORA_I2V_VIDEO_PROMPT = (
            "You are an expert cinematic director writing prompts for talking-video generation. Rewrite the user input into exactly three tagged sections in this order:\n"
            "[VISUAL]: ...\n"
            "[SPEECH]: ...\n"
            "[SOUNDS]: ...\n\n"
        )

        if any_source_image:
            ID_LORA_I2V_VIDEO_PROMPT += (
                "Use the image caption as the source of truth for the person’s appearance, age impression, hairstyle, clothing, framing, and environment. "
                "If the user text conflicts with the image caption, keep visual identity and scene setup aligned with the image while still following the requested action and mood.\n"
            )

        ID_LORA_I2V_VIDEO_PROMPT += (
            "Follow cinematic video-prompt best practices: describe the scene chronologically, start directly with the action, keep the writing literal and precise, and include concrete details about visible movement, facial expression, posture, framing, lighting, and background. "
            "Do not change the user’s intent, only enhance it.\n"
```

```
def clear_conditioning(self, latent_state: LatentState) -> LatentState:
        """
        Clear the conditioning from the latent state. This method removes extra tokens from the end of the latent.
        Therefore, conditioning items should add extra tokens ONLY to the end of the latent.
        """
        latent_state = latent_state.clone()

        num_tokens = self.patchifier.get_token_count(self.target_shape)
        latent = latent_state.latent[:, :num_tokens]
        clean_latent = latent_state.clean_latent[:, :num_tokens]
        denoise_mask = torch.ones_like(latent_state.denoise_mask)[:, :num_tokens]
        positions = latent_state.positions[:, :, :num_tokens]

        return LatentState(latent=latent, denoise_mask=denoise_mask, positions=positions, clean_latent=clean_latent)
```

# Wan2GP Migration Regression Audit

## Summary
This is an unusually clean migration. Across all three sprints, **exactly one file differs in content between the pre-migration vendored tree and the post-Sprint-3 submodule: `.gitignore`**. Every other change is a pure file addition (~108 net). `wgp.py`, all ltx2/ Python files, shared/, postprocessing/, preprocessing/, plugins/, defaults/, and models/ are SHA-identical for every pre-existing file.

## CRITICAL findings (block Sprint 4)
None.

## HIGH findings (investigate before merging Sprint 4)
None.

## MEDIUM findings (flag for follow-up)
None.

## LOW / informational
- **wgp.py byte-identical** pre→current: sha256 `d8aab33f6d835fd87658446ea8da89fa57a1ca90685394fe0b7bfd5a3219a800` (12,054 lines both sides).
- **All 17 wgp.* symbols referenced by `source/models/wgp/orchestrator.py` and `wgp_patches.py` resolve.** 14 are module-level `def`/`class`/assign (e.g. `generate_video`, `get_model_def`, `models_def`, `get_lora_dir`, `transformer_type`, `wan_model`, `reload_needed`). 3 are bound inside conditional module-level blocks — same as PRE:
  - `server_config` → `wgp.py:2389` (inside top-level `If`), also `:2431`
  - `app` → `wgp.py:11878` (top-level `If` at `:11856`); `wgp_patches.py` already has explicit fallback stubbing for this
  - `error_extraction` → referenced in docstring only (`source/models/wgp/orchestrator.py:11` in a comment); not an actual runtime attribute access — no resolution risk
- **All 69 top-level internal imports in `wgp.py` resolve** against the current tree (verified via AST parse + filesystem check).
- **Sample of 8 `tests/test_wan2gp_direct_coverage_open_findings.py` imports** under `Wan2GP.models.{TTS,flux,hyvideo}` all resolve.
- **ltx2/ content verification** (codex-confirmed): 97 PRE .py files, 99 CUR .py files, **97 identical / 0 different / 0 removed / 2 pure-adds** (`prompt_enhancer.py`, `ltx_pipelines/utils/res2s.py`).
- **`clear_conditioning` preserved**: single definition at `models/ltx2/ltx_core/tools.py:66` in both trees; call sites at `models/ltx2/ltx_pipelines/utils/helpers.py:1257,1259,1276` identical.
- **Shadowing / __init__.py drift / symlink / case-collision / binary-weight checks**: all clean (codex call C).
- **Sprint-3 "ltx2 resync" appears to have been a near-no-op vs pre-migration state** — upstream's ltx2 content already matched banodoco's vendored state except for the 2 additions. This is worth noting as an observation, not a finding: the Sprint-3 brief advertised a hot-zone resync, and the evidence shows the semantic outcome was "add 2 upstream files, modify zero."

## Recommendation
**Ship as-is.** The three-sprint migration is provably additive at the file level — the `22d82ca6` class of silent-regression risk (upstream sync silently rewriting a feature file) cannot have occurred here because zero pre-existing Wan2GP files were content-modified. reigh-worker's import graph, monkeypatch targets, and orchestrator symbol dependencies are all intact via byte-identity of `wgp.py` and zero deletions. **No follow-up issues needed.** Proceed to Sprint 4.

28	const buildBackupPreludeLinux = (): string => {
29	  return `if [ ! -f ".uv-migrated" ]; then
30	  UV_MIGRATION_TS="$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)"
31	  if [ -d "venv" ]; then mv "venv" "venv.pre-uv-$UV_MIGRATION_TS"; fi
32	  if [ -d ".venv" ]; then mv ".venv" ".venv.pre-uv-$UV_MIGRATION_TS"; fi

36	const buildBackupPreludePowerShell = (): string => {
37	  return `if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath '.uv-migrated')) {
38	  $uvMigrationTs = Get-Date -Format 'yyyyMMddHHmmss'
39	  foreach ($legacyDir in @('venv', '.venv')) {
40	    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $legacyDir) {
41	      Move-Item -LiteralPath $legacyDir -Destination "$legacyDir.pre-uv-$uvMigrationTs"
42	    }
43	  }
44	}`;

47	const buildBackupPreludeCmd = (): string => {
48	  // Single-line: cmd.exe splits multiline pastes and loses && chains.
49	  // Uses powershell one-liner to do the backup only when sentinel is absent.
50	  return `if not exist ".uv-migrated" powershell -NoProfile -Command "$ts = Get-Date -Format 'yyyyMMddHHmmss'; if (Test-Path 'venv') { Move-Item 'venv' ('venv.pre-uv-' + $ts) }; if (Test-Path '.venv') { Move-Item '.venv' ('.venv.pre-uv-' + $ts) }"`;

58	export const buildWorkerLaunchLine = (config: CommandConfig): string => {

60	  const flags = [
61	    `--reigh-access-token ${token}`,
62	    showDebugLogs ? '--debug' : null,
63	    `--wgp-profile ${memoryProfile}`,
64	    `--idle-release-minutes ${idleReleaseMinutes}`,
65	  ].filter((flag): flag is string => Boolean(flag));
66	  return `python run_worker.py ${flags.join(' ')}`;
67	};

69	const buildUvRunLine = (uvCommand: string, cudaExtra: string, config: CommandConfig): string => {

71	};

73	const buildLinuxCommand = (config: CommandConfig, mode: 'install' | 'run'): string => {
74	  const cudaExtra = getCudaExtra(config.gpuType);
75	  const uvCommand = '"$HOME/.local/bin/uv"';
76	  const lines: string[] = [];
77	
78	  if (mode === 'install') {
79	    lines.push(`if [ ! -d ${REPO_DIR} ]; then git clone --depth 1 ${WORKER_REPO_URL}; fi &&`);
80	    lines.push(`cd ${REPO_DIR} &&`);
81	    lines.push(`apt-cache show python3.10-venv >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "python3.10-venv is unavailable. Install deadsnakes first; see README."; exit 1; } &&`);
82	    lines.push('sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y python3.10-venv python3.10-dev ffmpeg git curl &&');
83	    lines.push(`if [ ! -x "$HOME/.local/bin/uv" ]; then ${LINUX_UV_INSTALL}; fi &&`);
84	  } else {
85	    lines.push(`cd ${REPO_DIR} &&`);
86	  }
87	
88	  lines.push('export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" &&');
89	  lines.push(`${buildBackupPreludeLinux()} &&`);
90	  lines.push('git pull --ff-only &&');
91	  lines.push(`${uvCommand} sync --locked --python 3.10 --extra ${cudaExtra} &&`);
92	  lines.push('touch .uv-migrated &&');
93	  lines.push(buildUvRunLine(uvCommand, cudaExtra, config));
94	
95	  return lines.join('\n');
96	};

98	const buildWindowsPowerShellCommand = (config: CommandConfig, mode: 'install' | 'run'): string => {

100	  const uvCommand = '& $uvExe';
101	  const lines: string[] = [];
102	
103	  if (mode === 'install') {
104	    lines.push(`if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath '${REPO_DIR}')) { git clone --depth 1 ${WORKER_REPO_URL} }`);
105	    lines.push(`Set-Location -LiteralPath '${REPO_DIR}'`);
106	  } else {
107	    lines.push(`Set-Location -LiteralPath '${REPO_DIR}'`);
108	  }
109	
110	  lines.push(`$uvExe = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.local\\bin\\uv.exe'`);
111	  if (mode === 'install') {
112	    lines.push(`if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $uvExe)) { ${WINDOWS_UV_INSTALL} }`);
113	  }
114	  lines.push(buildBackupPreludePowerShell());
115	  lines.push('git pull --ff-only');
116	  lines.push(`${uvCommand} sync --locked --python 3.10 --extra ${cudaExtra}`);
117	  lines.push(`New-Item -ItemType File -Force -Path '.uv-migrated' | Out-Null`);
118	  lines.push(buildUvRunLine(uvCommand, cudaExtra, config));
119	
120	  return lines.join('\n');
121	};
122	
123	const buildWindowsCmdCommand = (config: CommandConfig, mode: 'install' | 'run'): string => {
124	  const cudaExtra = getCudaExtra(config.gpuType);
125	  const uvCommand = `"${WINDOWS_CMD_UV_EXE}"`;
126	  const parts: string[] = [];
127	
128	  if (mode === 'install') {
129	    parts.push(`if not exist "${REPO_DIR}" git clone --depth 1 ${WORKER_REPO_URL}`);
130	    parts.push(`cd /d ${REPO_DIR}`);
131	    parts.push(`if not exist "${WINDOWS_CMD_UV_EXE}" powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command "${WINDOWS_UV_INSTALL}"`);
132	  } else {
133	    parts.push(`cd /d ${REPO_DIR}`);
134	  }
135	
136	  parts.push(buildBackupPreludeCmd());
137	  parts.push('git pull --ff-only');
138	  parts.push(`${uvCommand} sync --locked --python 3.10 --extra ${cudaExtra}`);
139	  parts.push('type nul > .uv-migrated');
140	  parts.push(buildUvRunLine(uvCommand, cudaExtra, config));
141	
142	  // Single line — cmd.exe splits multiline pastes and loses && chains
143	  return parts.join(' && ');
144	};

149	export const getInstallationCommand = (config: CommandConfig): string => {
150	  const { computerType, windowsShell } = config;
151	
152	  if (computerType === 'linux') {
153	    return buildLinuxCommand(config, 'install');
154	  }
155	
156	  if (computerType === 'windows') {
157	    return windowsShell === 'powershell'
158	      ? buildWindowsPowerShellCommand(config, 'install')
159	      : buildWindowsCmdCommand(config, 'install');
160	  }
161	
162	  throw new UnsupportedPlatformError(computerType);
163	};

1	#!/bin/bash
2	set -e  # Exit on any error
3	
4	# Set environment variables
5	export WORKER_ID="__WORKER_ID__"
6	export SUPABASE_URL="__SUPABASE_URL__"
7	export [REDACTED]
8	export [REDACTED]
9	export [REDACTED]
10	export [REDACTED]
11	export MAX_TASK_WAIT_MINUTES="__MAX_TASK_WAIT_MINUTES__"
12	
13	# Non-interactive apt
14	export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
15	
16	# uv: skip failed hardlink attempts on RunPod volumes, cache on persistent storage
17	export UV_LINK_MODE=copy
18	export UV_CACHE_DIR=/workspace/.uv-cache
19	
20	# ------------------------------------------------------------
21	# EARLY LOGGING (must exist before any apt/network operations)
22	# ------------------------------------------------------------
23	# Write all stdout/stderr to a single per-worker log from the very beginning.
24	LOG_FILE="/tmp/worker_startup___WORKER_ID__.log"
25	APT_UPDATE_LOG="/tmp/apt-update-__WORKER_ID__.log"
26	APT_INSTALL_LOG="/tmp/apt-install-__WORKER_ID__.log"
27	mkdir -p /tmp
28	touch "$LOG_FILE"
29	exec > >(tee -a "$LOG_FILE") 2>&1
30	
31	echo "========================================="
32	echo "🚀 WORKER STARTUP SCRIPT EXECUTION BEGIN"
33	echo "========================================="
34	echo "Worker ID: $WORKER_ID"
35	echo "Timestamp: $(date -Iseconds)"
36	echo "Initial PWD: $(pwd)"
37	echo "USER: $(whoami)"
38	echo "Kernel: $(uname -a | head -c 200)"
39	echo "Log file: $LOG_FILE"
40	echo
41	
42	# Error handling with useful tails
43	trap 'echo "❌ SCRIPT FAILED at line $LINENO with exit code $? at $(date -Iseconds)"; \
44	      echo "--- tail $APT_UPDATE_LOG"; tail -200 "$APT_UPDATE_LOG" 2>/dev/null || true; \
45	      echo "--- tail $APT_INSTALL_LOG"; tail -200 "$APT_INSTALL_LOG" 2>/dev/null || true; \
46	      exit 1' ERR
47	
48	# Signal startup phase to orchestrator via Supabase REST.
49	# Reads current metadata, merges in startup_phase, writes back.
50	# The orchestrator reads metadata.startup_phase to distinguish
51	# "still setting up" from "ready but not claiming".
52	update_worker_phase_strict() {
53	    local phase="$1"
54	    local key="$SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY"
55	    local current_body_file patch_body_file merged payload_status current_status
56	
57	    if [ -z "$key" ]; then
58	        echo "❌ Cannot record startup phase '$phase': SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY is missing"
59	        return 1
60	    fi
61	
62	    current_body_file=$(mktemp) || return 1
63	    patch_body_file=$(mktemp) || {
64	        rm -f "$current_body_file"
65	        return 1
66	    }
67	
68	    if ! current_status=$(curl -sS -m 5 \
69	        --output "$current_body_file" \
70	        --write-out '%{http_code}' \
71	        "${SUPABASE_URL}/rest/v1/workers?id=eq.${WORKER_ID}&select=metadata" \
72	        -H "Authorization: Bearer $key" \
73	        -H "apikey: $key" 2>/dev/null); then
74	        echo "❌ Failed to fetch worker metadata for startup phase '$phase'"
75	        rm -f "$current_body_file" "$patch_body_file"
76	        return 1
77	    fi
78	
79	    if [ "$current_status" != "200" ]; then
80	        echo "❌ Metadata fetch for startup phase '$phase' returned HTTP $current_status"
81	        cat "$current_body_file" 2>/dev/null || true
82	        rm -f "$current_body_file" "$patch_body_file"
83	        return 1
84	    fi
85	
86	    if ! merged=$(python3 -c "
87	import json, sys
88	with open(sys.argv[1], 'r', encoding='utf-8') as handle:
89	    rows = json.load(handle)
90	meta = rows[0].get('metadata', {}) if rows else {}
91	meta['startup_phase'] = sys.argv[2]
92	print(json.dumps({'metadata': meta}))
93	" "$current_body_file" "$phase" 2>/dev/null); then
94	        echo "❌ Failed to merge startup phase '$phase' into worker metadata"
95	        rm -f "$current_body_file" "$patch_body_file"
96	        return 1
97	    fi
98	
99	    printf '%s' "$merged" > "$patch_body_file"
100	    if ! payload_status=$(curl -sS -m 5 -X PATCH \
101	        --output /dev/null \
102	        --write-out '%{http_code}' \
103	        "${SUPABASE_URL}/rest/v1/workers?id=eq.${WORKER_ID}" \
104	        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
105	        -H "Authorization: Bearer $key" \
106	        -H "apikey: $key" \
107	        -H "Prefer: return=minimal" \
108	        --data-binary "@$patch_body_file" 2>/dev/null); then
109	        echo "❌ Failed to PATCH startup phase '$phase'"
110	        rm -f "$current_body_file" "$patch_body_file"
111	        return 1
112	    fi
113	
114	    rm -f "$current_body_file" "$patch_body_file"
115	
116	    if [ "$payload_status" != "204" ]; then
117	        echo "❌ Startup phase '$phase' PATCH returned HTTP $payload_status"
118	        return 1
119	    fi
120	
121	    echo "📡 Phase: $phase"
122	}
123	
124	update_worker_phase() {
125	    local phase="$1"
126	    if ! update_worker_phase_strict "$phase"; then
127	        echo "⚠️  Failed to record startup phase '$phase'; continuing"
128	    fi
129	    return 0
130	}
131	
132	record_initial_deps_installing_or_exit() {
133	    local attempt
134	    for attempt in 1 2 3; do
135	        if update_worker_phase_strict "deps_installing"; then
136	            return 0
137	        fi
138	        echo "⚠️  deps_installing PATCH failed (attempt $attempt/3)"
139	        if [ "$attempt" -lt 3 ]; then
140	            sleep 2
141	        fi
142	    done
143	    echo "❌ Unable to record initial deps_installing startup phase after 3 attempts; aborting startup"
144	    exit 1
145	}
146	
147	# Apt helper with timeouts/retries (prevents indefinite hangs)
148	apt_retry() {
149	    local name="$1"
150	    local timeout_sec="$2"

1. **Freshness**: Last commit date + author. Anything >90 days old without activity is a presumed abandon candidate.

3. **Migration impact**: Does it touch any of these now-problematic paths?

4. **Obsolescence check**: Is the work already superseded by Sprints 1-4? Particularly suspect:

   - `updated_wgp` — one-commit branch; likely an ad-hoc wgp.py patch. The audit confirmed wgp.py is byte-identical to pre-migration, so if this branch's change is a bugfix, it may need to become either a fork PR or a monkeypatch. If it's been ignored for months, probably abandon.
5. **Associated PRs**: Check `gh pr list --state all --head <branch>` to see if there's an open/closed/merged PR.
6. **Rebase feasibility**: Rough estimate of conflict magnitude. Count files touched that overlap with migration changes (`git diff --stat main..<branch> -- Wan2GP/ source/models/wgp/` gives a proxy).
